key_insight: A PDE foundation model (Poseidon) pretrained on diverse numerical PDE solutions can be extended from 2D to 3D and fine-tuned to become a skillful, physics-aware weather emulator for the Martian atmosphere while retaining pretraining knowledge.
problem_solved: How to adapt a 2D PDE foundation model to produce accurate, efficient 3D atmospheric forecasts for Mars without discarding the physics information learned during pretraining.
method: Use the Poseidon PDE foundation model pretrained on a diverse corpus of 2D PDE numerical solutions as the starting point.
Develop and apply a model-extension strategy to lift the pretrained 2D representations to 3D while preserving learned inductive biases from pretraining.
Fine-tune the 3D-extended model on Martian atmospheric data/simulations to produce a fast, skillful weather emulator.
impact: Provides a pathway to fast, physics-informed planetary weather emulators that reduce reliance on costly full numerical simulators—accelerating research, mission planning, and iterative model development for AI/ML practitioners working in geophysical and planetary domains.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram showing '2D Poseidon pretraining' → '3D extension method' → 'Fine-tuned Martian emulator' (flowchart)
Side-by-side comparison plot of emulator forecast vs. reference numerical model for a representative Martian variable (e.g., pressure or wind) to illustrate fidelity
Illustration of model architecture adaptation (layers or tensors expanding from 2D to 3D) highlighting preserved pretrained weights
Icons: Mars planet, PDE/math symbols, and a speedometer or clock to convey computational speedup
paper_title: PDE foundation models are skillful AI weather emulators for the Martian atmosphere
paper_authors: Johannes Schmude, Sujit Roy, Liping Wang, Theodore van Kessel, Levente Klein
